summary: Name-based hash-table lookup (thiscall on the bucket array). If the caller passes hash -1 the key string is hashed via StringHash; a -1 hash result fails immediately. Otherwise the table entry at index a3 (the hash) is taken as the head of a collision chain and walked by comparing each node's name pointer (node+16, falling back to global byte_5EA438 when null) against the key with sub_588410; the first matching node is returned, and 0 is returned when the chain ends without a match. Canonical and ABI names both describe a hash-table lookup by name.

operations.description: When the supplied hash a3 equals -1, compute the hash by calling StringHash(a2); if that also returns -1 the lookup fails immediately with 0.
v5 = this[v3]: dereference the bucket array at the resolved hash index to obtain the head of the collision chain.
If the chain head v5 is null, return 0 (no entry for this hash).

Walk the collision chain: read the node name pointer at node+16 (falling back to the global default string byte_5EA438 when null), compare it to the key a2 via sub_588410 and break on a match, then advance to the next node at node+4; a null next node ends the walk with 0.
Return the matching chain node, or 0 when the hash is -1, the bucket is empty, or the chain is exhausted; the function is invoked by AudioChannelStop to resolve an audio channel by name.

unresolved: The exact comparison convention of sub_588410 (whether a 0 return means equal, as assumed here) is not grounded by this packet.
The role and content of the fallback global byte_5EA438 used when a node has no name pointer are unknown.
The bucket-array layout behind `this` (how many buckets, stride, and how the array is owned) is outside this packet.
